subject.title: chore(deps): bump the actions group across 1 directory with 14 updates

question: Should OpenClaw trust and adopt these grouped upstream Action revisions in workflows that handle credentials, publishing, security scanning, repository mutation, and agent execution?
rationale: The patch itself is mechanically sound, but approving new executable upstream code at privileged boundaries is an owner trust decision, and the repository's mandatory direct Codex-source gate remains incomplete.

options.title: Approve after full trust review
options.body: Verify the upstream revisions and exact Codex contract, rebase, and require clean exact-head checks before merge.

options.title: Split privileged families
options.body: Separate Codex, token, Docker publishing, CodeQL, and repository-maintenance Actions into smaller PRs for narrower trust review.

options.title: Retain current pins
options.body: Pause or close the grouped update if owners cannot establish adequate upstream and exact-head proof.

recommendation.title: Approve after full trust review
recommendation.body: Verify the upstream revisions and exact Codex contract, rebase, and require clean exact-head checks before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: This team is the explicit CODEOWNER for several security-sensitive workflows changed by the PR and is best positioned to approve the new executable revisions.
